DialogLine.Friendly: Greetings. I speak for the Dominion, and for the Founders, who are pleased to make your acquaintance. It is an honour, truly.
DialogLine.Neutral: The Dominion greets you. I am a Vorta, and I speak for the Founders. I hope this meeting will be agreeable to everyone.
DialogLine.Hostile: So you are the PLURAL. The Founders were curious, and I confess I am rather unimpressed. You should hope that does not change.

DialogLine.Friendly: Forgive me, but the Founders have noticed your colony in TARSYS. I am sure it was an oversight. I would hate to see it become a problem.
DialogLine.Neutral: SING, your colony in TARSYS stands in the Dominion's way. The Founders would be most displeased if it remained there.
DialogLine.Hostile: You settle TARSYS, a system that the Dominion has marked as its own? The Founders will not forget your arrogance.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your ships have fired on ours. Surely there has been a misunderstanding? I would so like to avoid reporting this to the Founders.
DialogLine.Neutral: You have attacked Dominion ships, SING. The Founders do not look kindly on that.
DialogLine.Hostile: You attack the Dominion, PLURAL? That was a very bad idea, and I cannot imagine what you were thinking.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your ships have been in our space for some time. I'm certain you mean no harm, but I must ask you to withdraw them.
DialogLine.Neutral: PLURAL ships in Dominion space. The Jem'Hadar are growing impatient, and so, I am afraid, am I.
DialogLine.Hostile: Your ships are in Dominion space, PLURAL. Leave at once, or the Jem'Hadar will remove them. They are very good at it.

DialogLine.Friendly: We asked you to leave our space, and you stayed. Now you take TARSYS. I am afraid the Founders are very disappointed.
DialogLine.Neutral: You ignored our warning and settled TARSYS. The Founders do not take kindly to being ignored, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: You trespassed, you were warned, and now you take TARSYS. The Founders will not be patient any longer.

DialogLine.Friendly: You settled TARSYS and we said nothing, and now you bring warships. The Founders are growing concerned.
DialogLine.Neutral: First TARSYS, and now warships at our borders. The Founders are beginning to see a pattern, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: You took TARSYS, and now you threaten our borders. The Founders will answer, and the Jem'Hadar will carry it out.

Dialogs.DialogLine: Declare War The Founders have decided. The Dominion is at war with you. Order will be restored, one world at a time. The Jem'Hadar are on their way. For them, victory is life. For you, I am afraid, the opposite.>

DialogLine.Default: There are others out there? How fascinating. The Founders will want to hear of it. We have not yet met them.

DialogLine.Friendly: Ah, an old friend! The Founders will be so pleased to hear from you. What can I do for you?
DialogLine.Neutral: I'm listening, SING. I do hope this will not take too long.
DialogLine.Hostile: Yes? Speak. The Founders have more important matters, and so do I.

DialogLine.Default: Fascinating. Your people are not what the Founders expected. Tell me more about yourselves.
I see. The Founders will be interested to hear it.

DialogLine.DL_Agg: The Dominion does not start wars, as a rule. It simply finishes them, and the Jem'Hadar are very, very good at finishing them.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: The Founders keep their word, and so do the Vorta. We would ask nothing less of you.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: The Dominion wishes only for order and peace. The best way to keep peace is to make sure everyone knows their place.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: The Founders have a great plan for the galaxy, and everyone has a place in it. Those who resist will find the Jem'Hadar waiting.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: A Vorta is bred to be clever, and loyal. I assure you I am both. You may trust me, in matters the Founders have approved.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: The Founders look upon solids with caution, and with good reason. We would not trust them with anything of importance.
DialogLine.DL_Exp: The Dominion's borders are wide, and the Founders have so much more to bring under their care. There is a great deal of order still to be made.
DialogLine.DL_Tech: The Founders' science is far beyond what you can imagine. The Dominion shares its gifts only with those it trusts.
DialogLine.DL_Mil: The Jem'Hadar number in the many thousands, and they do not fear death. I would recommend you do not test them.
DialogLine.DL_Ind: Order requires many ships and many hands. The Dominion has both, and it builds more every day.
DialogLine.DL_Gen: The Dominion is a great power, and a patient one. Order, peace and loyalty: that is what we offer. I would accept it, if I were you.

DialogLine.Default: I am afraid not. The Founders do not trust you enough for that.
You are very generous, SING, for a people who barely know us. The Founders accept, of course. They do like to be treated well.
I'm afraid this is a poor offer from a people we do not trust. The Founders decline.
The Founders hold you in some regard, so I will be honest: your offer is not good enough. I suggest you try again.
Another power holds worlds in that system, and the Dominion has no open borders with them. I am afraid the Founders cannot allow it.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: The Dominion chooses its own enemies, SING. It does not need your help.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: Solids meddling on our borders. The Founders have always had their doubts.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: To set neighbours against each other is a poor way to treat a friend. I am surprised.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: You would have us quarrel with our neighbours? The Founders prefer order to quarrels.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: A clever scheme, but the Dominion was playing such games before your people had a name.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: I can see the trap you have laid, SING. I am a Vorta, after all. We do not step into them.

DialogLine.Default: The Dominion's enemies hold worlds in that system, SING. The Founders do not wish your settlers caught up in the war.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: When the Dominion wants those worlds, the Jem'Hadar will take them.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: The Dominion has no use for solids' colonies on its battlefields.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: We will not put your settlers at risk on our account. It is a kind thought, and I thank you for it.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: We hope to end that war, not to spread it. Thank you, but no.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: Those worlds will be ours shortly, without your help.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: A world on the front line is more trouble than it is worth. Perhaps another time.

DialogLine.Default: I would call this offer an insult, but that suggests you intended something. The Founders decline.
A reasonable arrangement. The Founders approve. It is agreed.
A very good arrangement. The Founders are pleased. It is agreed.
You are far too generous, SING. The Founders accept, with their compliments.
A gift for the Founders? How thoughtful. They accept, naturally.
Your request is modest enough. The Founders grant it. I hope you will remember their kindness.
You expect the Dominion to bend to this? I would not push the matter, if I were you.
Very well. The Founders do not need to be quarrelsome over so small a matter.
A poor bargain, forced upon us. The Founders will remember it. They remember everything.
You make a pact with the Dominion and then break it? That was unwise. The Founders declare war.
It is war, then. The Founders had expected it, and the Jem'Hadar have been waiting.
We are at war, PLURAL. Say what you must, and quickly.
You bring warships to our border, and the Jem'Hadar will meet them. I do not expect a long engagement.
We warned you to leave Dominion territory, and you stayed. The Founders have chosen war, and I am afraid it is your doing.
You remain in TARSYS despite every warning, PLURAL. The Dominion is at war with you.
The Founders would prefer not to waste ships on needless wars. Perhaps a non-aggression pact would serve us both?
Wonderful. The Founders will be so pleased. The Dominion will honour this agreement, as long as you do.
You decline? Then the Founders will assume that you wish to remain open to other arrangements.
The Dominion is prepared to open its markets to you. The Founders believe that trade between our peoples would be most agreeable. Shall we sign a treaty?
Wonderful. The Founders are pleased, and I am delighted. Let our trade be profitable.
You turn down trade with the Dominion? The Founders will be disappointed. As am I, SING.
First you refuse a pact, and now you ask for one? The Founders do not like indecision.
You declined trade earlier. Now you ask for it. I confess I am curious as to what changed.
The Founders require TECH_DEMAND from you, SING. I would hate for our relations to suffer.
Thank you. The Founders appreciate a sensible partner. I do as well.
You refuse? How unfortunate. The Founders will take note.
The PLURAL fleet is rather small, isn't it? The Jem'Hadar will be disappointed at how little challenge it offers.
Your fleet is not without merit. The Founders have taken note, with interest.
You have improved your fleet, SING. How unfortunate. I will have to report it to the Founders.
You cannot defend your worlds, SING. The Dominion will take over for you, and bring them order.
The Kulrathi Shogunate is disciplined and loyal to its shogun. The Founders can appreciate that.
The Kulrathi keep to their warrior code. The Founders watch them, and the Kulrathi watch back. It is a fair arrangement.
The Kulrathi believe that their code makes them equals. The Jem'Hadar would be delighted to correct them.
The Pollops are gentle and obedient. They would make fine subjects of the Dominion, and I say it as a compliment.
The Pollops live quietly among their gardens. They are no concern of the Dominion, and I suspect they like it that way.
The Pollops talk of harmony while their worlds lie unguarded. They would be much happier under the Founders' care.
The Vulfen Imperium is loud, proud and loyal to its own. The Founders could do worse as a neighbour.
The Vulfen Imperium has not troubled the Dominion, and the Dominion has not troubled them. That may change.
The Vulfen Imperium is a pack of belligerent hunters who mistake noise for strength. The Jem'Hadar will teach them otherwise.
The Humans are noisy and sentimental, and the Founders find that oddly charming. We would like to keep them around.
The Humans are a young people with big ideas. The Founders have no fixed view of them. Yet.
The Humans insist on their freedom and their rights, as if either would save them. They are a threat to order.
The Ralyeh Devoted are patient, faithful and committed. The Founders can respect such devotion, especially when it is not aimed at them.
The Ralyeh keep to their faith and their waters. The Dominion does not meddle in faith, so long as it does not interfere with order.
The Ralyeh Devoted worship death, and they are eager to meet it. The Jem'Hadar would be happy to oblige.
You thought a treaty would keep the Dominion at bay? I do enjoy it when people are optimistic.
It is over, SING. The Dominion is victorious, and your worlds are now under the Founders' care. I am sure you will find order agreeable.
The PLURAL have been most agreeable, and the Founders see no harm in open borders. Shall we?
Wonderful. Our ships may pass in peace, and the Founders expect yours to do the same.
You refuse open borders? How disappointing. The Founders will keep watching, nonetheless.
We had a treaty, and you broke it, and for what? TARSYS? The Founders will not forget this betrayal. The Dominion is at war with you.
TARSYS belongs to the Dominion. You have invaded it. The Founders have declared war.
The Opteris are single-minded and tireless, and they do as they are told. What is there not to admire?
The Opteris are an odd people, half machine and half insect. The Founders find them interesting, but not important.
The Opteris are cold, and they answer to no one. That is a danger, and the Founders do not tolerate dangers.
TARSYS was claimed by the Dominion. You took it. The Founders do not overlook such things.

DialogLine.Friendly: Dear friend, the Dominion has claimed TARSYS. The Founders would be so grateful if you did not settle there.
DialogLine.Neutral: TARSYS is claimed by the Dominion. The Founders suggest you look elsewhere, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: TARSYS is within the Dominion's claim, PLURAL. Settle there, and the Jem'Hadar will remove your colony.

DialogLine.Default: We have only just met the PLURAL. The Founders are still forming their opinion.
The Dominion has no quarrel with the PLURAL. You have behaved well, and the Founders take note.
The Founders have some concerns about the PLURAL. I would be delighted to discuss them.
You have taken worlds that the Dominion had planned for itself. The Founders have noticed.
You have taken worlds that the Dominion had planned for itself. The Founders have noticed.
Your fleet has grown too large for comfort. The Founders worry about such things.
Your fleet is small, and a weak neighbour is a temptation. The Founders would rather not be tempted.
Your fleet is weak. The Dominion does not ally with those who cannot defend themselves.
Your fleet has grown too large for comfort. The Founders worry about such things.
You are allied with TAREMP, who are enemies of the Dominion. A curious choice of friends.
You remain allied with TAREMP, who are enemies of the Dominion. The Founders have noted it.
We have no great quarrel with you. The Founders would like it to stay that way.
The war goes very well, SING. You may wish to speak while there is still someone left to hear you.
The war has not gone as the Founders hoped. I am willing to hear what you have to say, SING.
TAREMP are enemies of the Dominion. The Founders invite you to join us. There will be rewards for those who help.
Wonderful. The Founders will be so pleased. Together we shall bring TAREMP to order.
You will not help us against TAREMP? The Founders will remember who stood with them.
The Draylok Council is shrewd and well organised. The Founders approve of a people who keep their house in order.
The Draylok change their faces and their minds. We watch them. They are not yet a concern.
The Draylok hide behind borrowed faces, and the Founders have never trusted a people who hide. We find it insulting.
This war has cost us both a great deal. The Founders are willing to discuss peace.
We are winning, SING, but the Founders see no profit in prolonging it. Make peace with us.
Neither of us can win this war. A sensible people would end it before more ships are lost.
The war has gone poorly for us. The Founders would accept peace, on reasonable terms.
We hold your worlds. Sign this treaty, and the Founders will end the war.
You hold the field, SING. Keep your worlds, and give us peace. The Founders will be patient.
You refuse peace? Then the war continues. The Founders are patient.
Very well. There will be peace between us. The Founders are satisfied.
A reasonable offer. The Founders accept. There will be peace.
Your offer is not good enough. The Founders will not accept peace on those terms.
You still hold worlds that the Dominion wants. There will be no peace.
The Founders will accept this peace, though it does not please them. Do not mistake it for friendship.
We were at war not long ago. The Founders have not forgotten, and neither should you.
The Dominion and the PLURAL understand each other so well. Perhaps it is time for a formal alliance. The Founders would be delighted.
Wonderful. The Founders welcome this alliance, and look forward to its fruits.
You decline an alliance with the Dominion? Perhaps you will think again.
This is needlessly complicated. If you want an alliance, propose one plainly.
The Founders do not sign treaties with strangers. Not yet. Perhaps once we have come to know one another better.
The Founders agree. The Dominion will stand with you, as long as you stand with us.
An alliance? The Founders have not yet decided that you deserve one.
We trusted our treaty, and you broke it. The Founders will not forget this betrayal.
No peace. The Founders intend to finish what they have started.
There has been little loss on either side. A sensible time for peace. The Founders agree.
You will not fight beside us? Then you are no ally of the Dominion. The alliance is at an end.
You have colonised TARSYS, and you have crossed the Dominion twice now. A third time would be unwise.
You have stolen from the Dominion too many times. The Founders' patience is at an end.
We know you are spying on us, SING. The Dominion is flattered, but I must ask you to stop.
We asked you to stop spying. The Founders do not like to repeat themselves.
You have spied on us again. All treaties between our peoples are cancelled.
We have captured your spy. He had a great deal to say, once the Jem'Hadar asked.
A spy among our allies? We caught your agent. Is this how the PLURAL treat friends?
You spy on us again, ally? Our alliance is at an end.
Friends should not close their borders to one another. Open yours to us, SING.
You keep your borders closed even to friends? The PLURAL are very careful.
We have only just met. The Founders do not join a federation with strangers.
We are not even allies. The Founders will not consider a federation until we are.
We are allies, and that is a good beginning. But a federation requires a longer history of trust.
Why should the Dominion follow you? We are the stronger power. If anything, you should join us.
The Founders have decided. The Dominion will stand with you in a federation, and bring order to the galaxy together. It is a great day.
Before we join you, the Founders ask a service. Destroy TAREMP, and we will consider it.
TAREMP is destroyed. The Founders are satisfied. The Dominion will join your federation.
You wish the Dominion to join your federation? The Founders do not even trust you.
We will join you, but you must first ally with our friends, TAREMP. Win their confidence, and speak to us again.
You have made allies of our friends. The Founders are pleased. The Dominion will join your federation.
You are not even at war with TAREMP. Why would the Dominion fight for you?
The Dominion is already at war with TAREMP. Were you not informed?
The Dominion stands with its allies. The Jem'Hadar will make war on TAREMP. Victory is life.
TAREMP is our ally. The Dominion does not break its word, even for a friend. I regret it.
Why should the Dominion fight for you, PLURAL? Our relations do not warrant such a favour.
The Founders have no appetite for war with TAREMP. They would prefer to settle matters without bloodshed.
TAREMP is formidable. The Founders do not choose such a war lightly. We decline.
The Founders agree. We have not much else to do just now, and war with TAREMP will be most useful.
The Founders are concerned that you cannot be trusted as an ally, SING. I hope you will correct that.
The Founders have revoked our open borders. We no longer trust your empire to keep them.
